transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Yes — a 4C on this Samsung means it has not detected enough water entering. With the drum still dry after a couple of minutes, the usual causes are the water tap not fully open, a squashed/kinked inlet hose, or grit/scale blocking the small inlet mesh filter. A failed inlet valve is possible, but comes after those checks. 1. Check the water tap feeding the machine is fully open, and that the inlet hose behind the machine is not kinked or trapped against the wall. Also check whether other cold taps in the property have normal flow. Poor flow elsewhere points to the water supply rather than the washer. 2. Switch the washer off, unplug it and turn the water tap off. Put a towel underneath, unscrew the inlet hose from the machine end, and look into the water inlet for the small mesh screen. If it has debris or scale on it, rinse/brush it gently clean; do not poke it hard or remove it with sharp tools. A blocked mesh is a common free fix. 3. Refit the hose securely, turn the tap back on and check there is no leak, then try a short programme. If it now fills, that was the cause. If the tap is fully open, the hose and mesh are clear, other cold taps are fine, and it still stays dry with 4C, the inlet valve or its control/level sensing needs testing. That is the point where an engineer is sensible rather than buying a part blindly.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Tap was open, hose isn't kinked and the kitchen cold tap is fine. Going to take the hose off and check the mesh filter now.

That is the right next check. Switch off and unplug the washer, turn the supply tap off, and keep a towel below the connection before undoing the hose. If the mesh has grit or scale on it, gently rinse or brush it clean, refit the hose, check for leaks, then retry a short programme. A blocked mesh would fit a dry drum and 4C. If it is clean and the machine still remains dry, the leading possibilities become restricted flow from that particular washing-machine tap/hose, or an inlet valve that is not opening. The next useful check would be to confirm the hose itself delivers a strong flow into a bucket with the machine disconnected; if it does, an engineer should test the inlet valve and its controls rather than replacing parts on guesswork.
Took the hose off and the mesh filter is clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. I'll clean it and refit it now, then retry.

That clogged mesh is very likely the cause of the 4C and dry drum: it was restricting the water entering the machine. Clean it gently, refit the hose with its washer in place, then turn the tap on slowly and check the connection stays dry. Run a short programme and see whether it starts filling normally. If it fills and the 4C stays away, no call-out is needed. If the mesh is clean but it still remains dry and returns 4C, the next possibilities are poor flow from that specific supply connection or an inlet valve that is not opening; at that point an engineer should test the valve and its controls rather than replacing parts on guesswork.

Cleaned it, refitted the hose and ran a short programme. It fills normally now and the 4C has gone. Water company were working in the street two days ago and the water ran brown briefly, if that's relevant.

That suggests it: the inlet mesh blockage was causing the 4C. The street water work and brief brown water are very likely where the grit came from. No engineer is needed if it continues to fill normally. For the next few washes, just keep an eye on the hose connection for any drip after it was refitted. If water work happens again or the supply runs discoloured, it is worth checking the inlet mesh promptly if filling becomes slow or 4C returns. Is there anything else you would like help with?
